 Quentin Grimes gives Lakers 47 reasons to believe in supporting cast
 By Sam Amico - November 18, 2026 
 The Lakers have spent much of their nine-game winning streak riding Luka Doncic . Tuesday, Quentin Grimes gave them a reminder that someone else can take over, too.
 Boy, did he ever.
 Grimes scored a career-high 47 points, including 21 in the fourth quarter, to rescue the Lakers in a 118-114 overtime win over the Hornets. With Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler sidelined, this was a night when Los Angeles needed somebody to do considerably more than fill a spot.
 Grimes delivered one of the biggest shooting performances in franchise history. His 10 three-pointers put him alongside Kobe Bryant as the only Lakers to reach that mark, as relayed by Daniel Starkand of Lakers Nation .
 That included the three that forced overtime. He also forced a turnover in the final minute of the extra period before adding two free throws.
 The Lakers (13-2) certainly had issues worth discussing. They struggled to finish defensive possessions without Kessler, played from behind and needed an enormous individual effort to escape at home.
 THE LAKERS HAVE THE BEST RECORD IN THE NBA. 🔥 https://t.co/txpSocklOS pic.twitter.com/uwNMXqu5xn 
 — Hoop Central (@TheHoopCentral) November 18, 2026 
 Those concerns fit into the larger questions about their fast start . Winning doesn’t mean everything is working. But not everything needs to work in November, and when it comes to the first several weeks of the season, the Lakers can hold their heads high.
 And finding another player who can carry the offense when Doncic sits is a pretty useful development. Nobody should pencil Grimes in for 47 every night. The Lakers would happily settle for another dependable scoring option when opponents load up on their star.
 Tuesday, they got considerably more. They’ll take that ninth straight win into Wednesday’s home matchup with the Jazz.
